newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Beef scare tramples Belgian fast-food chain profit.
newsitem.headline: Beef scare tramples Belgian fast-food chain profit.

text.p: Belgian fast-food chain Quick Restaurants SA said on Monday the scare over "mad cow" disease in Britain sent first half 1996 profits tumbling and it saw a 30 to 35 percent fall in net profit for the year.
"The mad-cow crisis caused a violent drop in the number of people visiting restaurants...on all the markets where Quick is present," the company said in a statement.

"This phenomenon has been amplified by the difficult economic context and by the (general) slowdown in consumption levels," it added. The company had announced in July that full year 1996 profits would be below 1995 levels.
First half consolidated net profit plunged to seven million francs from 147 million in the year ago period. Turnover totalled 10.35 billion versus 9.26 billion.

Quick reiterated forecast made in July that there would be a 10 to 12 percent rise in sales for the full year. Before then the company had been forecasting a 15 percent increase. Quick plans to open 60 new restaurants in the year as a whole.
Quick, which said it was always able to certify the quality and origin of the beef served at its restaurants, believed the fears about beef should progressively diminish.
"With the fast food market retaining all its potential for development, Quick expects to re-discover a more sustained rhythm of growth from 1997," the statement said.
Quick Restaurants SA is 57.44 percent owned retailer GIB Group.
